subject: MAP: Polaris evaluation & ramp schedule

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Polaris evaluation & ramp schedule

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan (draft) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial milestones so we can align on pricing and ramp commitments. Highlights: 

- 2-week POC (pilot): up to 100k tokens/day simulated workload; Redwood provides dedicated evaluation capacity and priority support.
- Production ramp phase (30 days post-POC): target 250k tokens/day with a temporary 15% evaluation discount for the first month.
- Commit milestone (90 days): customer can exercise a committed capacity commitment for lower unit-pricing; we propose a graduated discount based on sustained average token/day.
- Renewal uplift clause: if usage increases by >50% at renewal, a structured uplift/commit re-negotiation window with pre-agreed pricing tiers to avoid surprises.

I've included a short table in the attachment mapping milestones -> pricing triggers. The ask from your side: sign the MAP PDF (or confirm acceptance by reply), and we can lock in the evaluation capacity this week.

Attachments: Polaris_MAP_draft.pdf (draft MAP), SOW_draft.docx (workplan)

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment on Wed morning to walk the MAP and procurement steps?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com]
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@polaris-tech.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Polaris evaluation & ramp schedule

Thanks Evelyn — the draft looks sensible. A couple of questions before we loop procurement: 

1) The renewal uplift clause: can you clarify how the uplift is calculated? We want to avoid an open-ended price step if usage jumps during the term.
2) For the commit milestone discounts, can you provide an example price table (current list vs. committed tiers) so I can share with finance?
3) Our procurement team will need the SOW and the standard T&Cs; are you able to provide a procurement-ready bundle?

We can do Wed 10:30am PT for the alignment call.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee | Head of AI Integrations | Polaris Tech
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Polaris MAP questions (pricing examples + uplift mechanics)

Eve / Priyom — answering Samantha's bullets so we have a clear proposal for Wed: 

1) Renewal uplift mechanics: propose a tiered approach (keeps it predictable):
   - If average daily usage at renewal <= 25% increase vs. contracted baseline: no price change.
   - 25% < increase <= 50%: move up one pricing tier (small uplift, ~7%).
   - >50% increase: customer enters a reprovision window where we offer a higher committed capacity discount if they commit to a new tier; otherwise, apply a one-time uplift of 15% but offer a 60-day grace period to finalize new commit terms.

2) Example price table (high level):
   - On-demand: $0.0009/token
   - Committed tier A (>= 500k tokens/day sustained): $0.00072/token (20% off on-demand)
   - Committed tier B (>= 1M tokens/day sustained): $0.00063/token (30% off)

3) Procurement bundle: Priyom — can you prepare the procurement-ready SOW + standard T&Cs and upload to the Drive link? Also include a short note on data residency/KMS options for Polaris.

If Laura can sign off on the renewal uplift path, we should present it as a customer-friendly safety valve rather than a punitive step.

- Rishi
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Polaris MAP questions (procurement bundle)

Attached a procurement-ready bundle to the Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/Polaris/MAP-draft (Polaris_MAP_draft.pdf, SOW_draft.docx). Key callouts I added:
- Explicit trial capacity hours and support SLA during POC.
- Billing cadence: monthly with an initial credit for the POC discount.
- Renewal uplift process documented with the tier examples Rishi suggested.

Also flagging a potential concession: if Polaris signs a 12-month committed capacity at Tier A within 30 days of POC close, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 5% of their first month committed spend. Approvals from finance needed but this helps accelerate commit.

Priyom
Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks for the questions. We updated the MAP and procurement bundle to make the renewal uplift predictable and customer-friendly. Summary below: 

- Uplift mechanics (tiered): no change <=25% growth; +7% pricing tier for 25–50% growth; >50% triggers reprovision window (15% uplift if no new commit agreed within 60 days).
- Example pricing table included in the attachment (on-demand vs committed tiers).
- Incentive: sign 12-month Tier A within 30 days of POC close -> one-time onboarding credit (5% first-month committed spend).
- Next steps: Wed 10:30am PT call confirmed. I'll share the Drive link and MAP PDF live in the meeting so procurement can download.

Attachments: Polaris_MAP_draft.pdf (updated)

Best,
Evelyn
